title: Decide whether the offer surface should withhold project.activate on a policy-less store, given that the admission table cannot carry the fact without hiding the receipt refusal
description:
Filed by worker-2739fee7 on 2026-09-05 from task-d342a2b158764fefa8dbf2a5365e7bf7, which RULED this out of its own scope rather than smuggling it in. That row is DELIVERED without it and does NOT depend on this one — this is the residue its ruling deliberately left open.

THIS IS A DESIGN QUESTION, NOT "ADD THE LINE". Read the whole framing before planning, because the obvious one-line fix is measured and REFUSED.

THE STANDING FACT. `project.activate` has TWO prerequisite authorities in the daemon:
  1. the ADMISSION TABLE `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES` (apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:31-35), which refuses BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING via bootstrap-services.ts:257 and feeds the offer surface via affordance-read.ts:206,239;
  2. the MEASURED RECEIPTS: `policy` is a member of ACTIVATION_RECEIPT_MEMBERS (activation-receipts.ts:29), valued from the installed slice set — `if (refs.length === 0) return unmeasuredReceipt("policy", "no policy slices installed")` (activation-receipts-measure.ts:213) — refusing ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED @ DAEMON_ACTIVATION_RECEIPTS.

Authority 1 does not know about the policy. So `/affordances/read` ADVERTISES `project.activate` as READY on a policy-less store while the receipt layer will refuse it. The surface offers a step the command path rejects. That is the real defect this row owns.

WHY THE ONE-LINE FIX IS REFUSED, measured as a control/treatment pair at fixed HEAD e6d02867, not reasoned. Adding `"policy.install"` to `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["project.activate"]` does not add a prerequisite — it MOVES WHICH LAYER ANSWERS. The admission gate then replies first and the receipt layer is never reached:

  AssertionError: expected 'BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING' to be 'ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED'
    apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/activation-command-entry.test.ts:108

That arm ("refuses POLICY_UNMEASURED on a store where no policy is installed") is load-bearing by its own comment: it "separates a live override from a defaulted one, because a defaulted `installedPolicySliceRefs` produces this SAME code". Re-pointing it at BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING would retire the question rather than answer it (global rail 1). So a plan that just adds the line and re-points that test is REJECTED before it starts.

MEASURED FALLOUT OF THE ONE-LINE EDIT, carried forward so nobody pays for it twice:
- 39 daemon files go red.
- 33 share ONE root cause and one fix: a second shared seeder nobody enumerates — apps/daemon/src/recovery/restore-test-harness.ts:182 `seedReadyProject` (via send at :167), 445x "seeding project.activate failed: BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING". Every other seeder funnels through it: attempt-finalization-test-harness.ts:251, budget-settlement-fixtures.ts:116/156, foundation-registry-fixtures.ts:437/471. Note bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:747-750 IS already correctly ordered — it is simply not the only shared seeder, which is the trap.
- 4 files need real edits across 9 arms: bootstrap/activation-command-entry.test.ts:108; http/affordance-read.test.ts:125 (pins the literal `missing:` roster); activation/admission-gate-resolver.test.ts:753,775,967,981; daemon-foundation-command.test.ts:113,143,232.
- NOT caused by it (whole-suite red, targeted green): bootstrap-services.test.ts, daemon-entry-ops.test.ts.
- Minimum roster is 12 paths, past the 10-file plan ceiling — so this is a SPLIT at plan time, not a discovery at step 5.

MEASURING THIS AREA AT ALL. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` runs ~22 min and is FLAKY: two back-to-back baselines gave `17 failed | 416 passed` then `10 failed | 423 passed`, dominated by 30000 ms timeouts. A whole-suite delta is NOT admissible attribution here. Use targeted control/treatment pairs — seconds, not minutes:
  cd apps/daemon && npx vitest run --root . --config package.json --testTimeout=30000 <files>

WHAT ALREADY LANDED, do not redo it: task-d342a2b1 put `policy.install` into `ACTIVATION_CHAIN_KINDS` (apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activation-port.ts) and corrected `CHAIN_ORDER` (work-labels.ts), so the BROWSER chain now satisfies both authorities and a fresh store activates. This row is about the DAEMON'S OWN OFFER SURFACE lying to every other consumer.

OPTIONS TO WEIGH (none is ruled here):
(a) leave the table alone and have the offer surface consult the receipt measurement directly, so `project.activate` is offered as BLOCKED with `missing: ["policy.install"]` while the receipt layer keeps owning the refusal;
(b) add the table entry AND deliberately re-seat the protected refusal at a layer that stays reachable — only if you can show the "live override vs defaulted" distinction survives, which is the thing the current arm exists to prove;
(c) accept the divergence and document it at both authorities, on the grounds that duplicating a fact in two layers is what created the hazard.

Serena: `mem:gotcha-adding-policy-install-to-command-prerequisites-hides-the-receipt-refusal`, `mem:gotcha-command-prerequisites-has-two-hand-transcribed-browser-mirrors`.
definitionOfDone: The chosen option is STATED with its reason in the completion record, and the two rejected options are named with why. A plan that adds `"policy.install"` to COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["project.activate"] and re-points activation-command-entry.test.ts:108 at BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING is refused by this row's rail 1 — if that is nonetheless the answer, the record must show the live-override-vs-defaulted distinction is still provable somewhere.

`ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED` @ `DAEMON_ACTIVATION_RECEIPTS` remains REACHABLE for `project.activate` on a policy-less store. Prove it by running apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/activation-command-entry.test.ts targeted and quoting `Test Files N passed`; then mutate the production surface and quote the red, so the arm is shown non-vacuous (global rail 1).

A test asserts what `/affordances/read` says about `project.activate` on a store with NO policy installed — the exact status and the exact `missing[]` roster — so the surface can never again advertise READY for a command the receipt layer will refuse. Assert the roster as set equality, not `toContain`.

If COMMAND_PREREQUISITES is changed, EVERY consumer is enumerated in the plan's owned paths BEFORE submission (global rail 19 + 24), including the shared seeders named in the description; the measured minimum roster is 12 paths, so the plan must SPLIT rather than submit over the ceiling.

Gates quoted WITH their `Test Files N passed` count lines. For the daemon use TARGETED control/treatment pairs, not the ~22 min flaky whole suite, and say which files were run; a whole-suite delta is not admissible attribution here.
taskRails: The receipt refusal must stay REACHABLE. `project.activate` refusing ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED at DAEMON_ACTIVATION_RECEIPTS on a policy-less store is the daemon failing closed under the member's own code. Do not re-point activation-command-entry.test.ts:108 at BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING to make a table edit green — that arm separates a live override from a defaulted one and re-pointing it retires the question.

This row is a DESIGN RULING first. Do not open with the one-line table edit: it is already measured (39 daemon files red, 12-path minimum roster) and its layer hazard is the reason task-d342a2b1 refused it. Read that measurement before planning.
Do not re-fix the browser side. `ACTIVATION_CHAIN_KINDS` and `CHAIN_ORDER` already carry `policy.install` (task-d342a2b1). This row owns the daemon's offer surface.

implementationPlan.description:
THE RULING IS OPTION (a), IN ITS CHEAP FORM. Record it as a task comment before any byte moves — DoD 1 asks for the choice AND the reason, and the completion record must repeat it. Read the row description's framing first; it is accurate and this step only decides between the three options it names.

RULED: the OFFER SURFACE withholds `project.activate` while no `policy.install` is committed, reporting it BLOCKED with `policy.install` in its `missing[]`. `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES` is NOT touched. The receipt layer keeps owning the refusal.

WHY NOT (b) — the table edit. Measured at fixed HEAD e6d02867 by worker-2739fee7: it does not add a prerequisite, it MOVES WHICH LAYER ANSWERS, so `ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED` stops being reachable from the omit-the-step store and `activation-command-entry.test.ts:108` reds with `expected 'BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING' to be 'ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED'`. Cost: 39 daemon files red, minimum roster 12 paths (past the 10-file ceiling, so it forces a split), and it requires re-pointing a protected arm — refused by rail 1 and rail 2.

WHY NOT (c) — document the divergence. The divergence is the defect: the surface advertises READY for a command the command path refuses. Documenting it leaves the dead button shipped.

WHY (a) IS CHEAP HERE, and this is the measurement that makes the ruling rather than a preference. Option (a) as the description words it — "have the offer surface consult the receipt measurement directly" — is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE as written: receipt measurement is ASYNC and `measureBackup` (bootstrap/activation-receipts-measure.ts:148-169) performs a REAL SQLITE BACKUP TO DISK, while `readSurface`/`bootstrapSteps` (http/affordance-read.ts:195-258) are synchronous, and `/affordances/read` is a known hot path that already had to be repaired for latency. Putting a store backup on it would be a serious regression.

It does not need to. `bootstrapSteps` ALREADY holds `ledger` and already branches on `ledger.kinds.has(kind)` at :225. `ledger.kinds.has("policy.install")` answers "is a policy installed" from data the surface has in hand, synchronously, at zero added cost. The surface reaches the same verdict as the receipt for the case an operator can actually hit, without measuring anything.

STATE THE LIMITATION HONESTLY — do not gloss it, it is the point rail 1 protects. There are TWO ways the policy receipt goes unmeasured:
  CASE 1, no `policy.install` committed. The surface now sees this and withholds. Operator-reachable; this is what ships.
  CASE 2, `policy.install` committed but the daemon never wired `installedPolicySliceRefs` — it defaults to `[]` in the production bundle (bootstrap/activation-receipts-ports.ts:200), so the receipt is unmeasured anyway. The surface CANNOT see this without the async measurement, so it will still offer READY and the receipt layer will still refuse.
Case 2 is the "live override vs defaulted" distinction `activation-command-entry.test.ts:103-105` exists to preserve, and it is precisely why the fact must NOT be duplicated into the admission table. Say in the record that case 2 remains surface-invisible by design, and that the receipt layer remains its only authority.
implementationPlan.note: Ruling recorded as comment-d53a545640a04f62b309e3f2f32dd988: OPTION (a) in its cheap form — the offer surface withholds project.activate while no policy.install is committed; COMMAND_PREREQUISITES untouched; receipt layer keeps the refusal. (b) and (c) named and refused with the measured reasons. Re-measured the plan's premises at HEAD rather than trusting them (global rail 6): measureActivationReceipts/measurePolicy are async (activation-receipts-measure.ts:230,259), measureBackup awaits a real store copy via ports.backup->copyStore (activation-receipts-ports.ts:195), bootstrapSteps/readSurface are sync (affordance-read.ts:194-258) — so consulting the receipt measurement from the surface is structurally impossible, and ledger.kinds.has("policy.install") is the cheap equivalent for case 1. CORRECTION to the row description: the policy branch is activation-receipts-measure.ts:237, not :213 (stale by ~24 lines). Also confirmed COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["project.activate"] = [project.register, project.bind_repository, provider.probe] and COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["policy.install"] = [] (bootstrap-sequence.ts:31-37), and ChainStep.missing is `readonly string[]` (affordance-contract.ts:65) so a non-table member is type-legal. Case 2 (policy committed, installedPolicySliceRefs unwired, defaults to []) stays surface-invisible by design — stated in the record. No files modified in this step.

implementationPlan.description:
RED ARMS FIRST, in apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.test.ts. Write them and watch them FAIL before the gate exists. The suite's `step(kind)` helper (:117-121) and `surface()` already give you the frame.

  1. THE DEFECT ARM (DoD 3). On a ledger where `project.register`, `project.bind_repository` and `provider.probe` are committed but `policy.install` is NOT, `step("project.activate")` is BLOCKED and its `missing` equals `["policy.install"]` — assert SET EQUALITY on the roster, not `toContain`. DoD 3 says this explicitly, and `toContain` would stay green if the roster later grew a bogus member.
  2. THE OFFER IS ACTUALLY WITHHELD. On that same frame, `nextAllowedCommands` does NOT contain `project.activate`. The step status and the offer roster must agree — a BLOCKED step beside a live offer is the exact split this row exists to close, so assert both on ONE frame rather than in two tests.
  3. THE CONVERSE, so the gate is not simply always-off. With `policy.install` ALSO committed, `step("project.activate")` is READY with `missing: []` AND `nextAllowedCommands` DOES contain `project.activate`. Without this arm a gate that withholds unconditionally passes arms 1 and 2.
  4. ORDER INDEPENDENCE. `policy.install` has no prerequisites (`COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["policy.install"]` is `[]`, bootstrap-sequence.ts:29) so it can commit at any point in the chain. Assert a world where policy is installed FIRST, before `project.register`, still reaches READY — the gate must test committed-ness, never position.
  5. THE OTHER KINDS ARE UNTOUCHED. `goal.create` still reports `missing: ["project.activate"]`. The gate must not leak into the generic `missingPrerequisites` path that every other kind uses.

Assert against the production surface. Do not build a helper that re-derives the roster.

I did NOT, because that frame is bound to ONE module-level store that every describe mutates in sequence, and `policy.install` is committed on it at :224 by the second describe. A late arm on the shared store could never observe "no policy installed" — it would have been green for the wrong reason and silently order-dependent. Each arm now opens its OWN tmpdir store via `policyWorld()` and drives the PRODUCTION `createAffordancePort(...).readSurface()`; no roster is re-derived anywhere.

ARMS AND WHAT EACH PINS: (1) defect arm — table prerequisites all committed, policy not: BLOCKED with `missing` SET-EQUAL to ["policy.install"] via toMatchObject array equality (not toContain, per DoD 3), PLUS `nextAllowedCommands` lacks project.activate on the SAME frame, PLUS goal.create still reports ["project.activate"] so the gate cannot leak into the generic missingPrerequisites path; then the CONVERSE on that same world — install the policy and it must go READY and be offered. (3) order independence — policy installed FIRST, before project.register, still READY (the gate tests committed-ness, never chain position). comments.content:
STEP 1 — THE RULING (DoD 1). Recorded before any byte moves.

**RULED: OPTION (a), in its cheap form.** The daemon's OFFER SURFACE withholds `project.activate` while no `policy.install` is committed: the step reports BLOCKED with `policy.install` in its `missing[]`, and the kind is absent from `nextAllowedCommands`. `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES` is NOT touched. The receipt layer keeps owning the refusal.

**WHY NOT (b) — the table edit.** Measured by worker-2739fee7 at fixed HEAD e6d02867: adding `"policy.install"` to `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["project.activate"]` does not add a prerequisite, it MOVES WHICH LAYER ANSWERS. The admission gate then replies first, `ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED @ DAEMON_ACTIVATION_RECEIPTS` stops being reachable from the omit-the-step store, and `activation-command-entry.test.ts` reds with `expected 'BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING' to be 'ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED'`. Cost: 39 daemon files red, minimum roster 12 paths (past the 10-file ceiling, so it forces a split), and it requires re-pointing a protected arm. Refused by this row's rails 1 and 2.

**WHY NOT (c) — document the divergence.** The divergence IS the defect: the surface advertises READY for a command the command path refuses. Documenting it ships the dead button.

**WHY (a) IS CHEAP HERE — measured, not preferred.** Option (a) as the description words it, "have the offer surface consult the receipt measurement directly", is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE as written, and I re-measured this rather than taking the plan's word:
- `measureActivationReceipts` and every member measurer are `async` (`bootstrap/activation-receipts-measure.ts:230,259`), and `measureBackup` performs a REAL STORE COPY to disk — `outcome = await ports.backup(input.storePath, destination)`, wired to `copyStore` in the production bundle (`activation-receipts-ports.ts:195`).
- `bootstrapSteps` / `readSurface` (`http/affordance-read.ts:194-258`) are SYNCHRONOUS, and `/affordances/read` is a known hot path that already needed a latency repair. Putting a sqlite backup on it would be a serious regression.

It does not need to. `bootstrapSteps` already holds `ledger` and already branches on `ledger.kinds.has(kind)` at :224. `ledger.kinds.has("policy.install")` answers "is a policy installed" from data the surface has in hand, synchronously, at zero added cost, and reaches the same verdict as the receipt for the case an operator can actually hit.

**THE LIMITATION, STATED HONESTLY — this is the part rail 1 protects.** There are TWO ways the policy receipt goes unmeasured:
- **CASE 1 — no `policy.install` committed.** `installedPolicySliceRefs()` returns empty, so `activation-receipts-measure.ts:237` answers `unmeasuredReceipt("policy", "no policy slices installed")`. The surface now sees this and withholds. Operator-reachable. This is what ships.
- **CASE 2 — `policy.install` committed but the daemon never wired `installedPolicySliceRefs`.** It defaults to `() => Promise.resolve([])` in the production bundle (`activation-receipts-ports.ts:200`), so the receipt is unmeasured anyway. The surface CANNOT see this without the async measurement, so it will still offer READY and the receipt layer will still refuse.

**Case 2 remains surface-invisible BY DESIGN, and the receipt layer remains its only authority.** That is exactly the "live override vs defaulted" distinction `activation-command-entry.test.ts:97-112` exists to preserve — its own comment says a defaulted `installedPolicySliceRefs` "produces this SAME code on the store above too" — and it is precisely why the policy fact must NOT be duplicated into the admission table.

Line numbers in the row description are STALE by ~24 lines in `activation-receipts-measure.ts` (the policy branch is at :237, not :213); re-measured at HEAD per global rail 6. The description's substance is otherwise accurate.

Note for the record: `bootstrap-sequence.ts` is dirty in the shared tree with a PEER session's work. This row does not touch it, which is consistent with the ruling.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE GATE THAT WITHHOLDS UNCONDITIONALLY. Arms 1 and 2 pass for a gate that always blocks `project.activate`. Arm 3 (policy committed -> READY and offered) is the only thing separating a fix from a regression that makes activation permanently unreachable — which would be the same dead-end failure the sibling row task-ebbcbdb4 exists to undo. The drill inverts the condition to prove arm 3 bites.

2. TIDYING THE GATE INTO THE TABLE. The next reader's instinct on seeing one kind gated outside `missingPrerequisites` is to move it into `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES`, which reintroduces the exact 39-file layer hazard. The plan requires an in-file comment naming the receipt member and the measurement so the question is answered permanently at the site.

3. CASE 2 OVERCLAIM. A completion record that says "the surface no longer advertises a command the receipt layer will refuse" would be FALSE: a daemon with `installedPolicySliceRefs` unwired still gets READY plus a refusal. The record must scope the claim to case 1.

4. SOFTENING THE PINNED LITERAL. The easy way to fix affordance-read.test.ts:126 is `toContain`; that would leave the roster unguarded, and DoD 3 explicitly demands set equality.

5. TOUCHING A LOOK-ALIKE LITERAL. Two files carry the same three-kind literal as a SEQUENCE roster (demo-seed-plan.test.ts:342, admission-witness-fixtures.ts:62). They must not move. Step 4 names them so a worker doing a blind find-and-replace is stopped at plan time rather than at review.

6. THE DAEMON SUITE IS NOT ADMISSIBLE ATTRIBUTION HERE. ~22 min and flaky (17 vs 10 failures across two back-to-back baselines, dominated by 30000ms spawn-latency timeouts). DoD 5 requires targeted control/treatment pairs and the named files; a whole-suite delta proves nothing about a three-file diff.

7. THE MUTATION IN STEP 5 IS ON PRODUCTION CODE, not a test. `activation-receipts-measure.ts` is tracked, so `git diff` is a valid restore proof — but it must be run in a call separate from the restore, and an unrestored mutation here would silently disarm the daemon's fail-closed policy receipt.
